name: Chinese New Left
summary: The Chinese New Left is a loose set of PRC intellectual currents, emerging in the 1990s, that criticize the market-oriented reform era for inequality, privatization and subordination to global capital while mostly keeping a market economy inside a socialist framework. Its adherents defend public ownership, state capacity, rural and regional equity and economic democracy, view the Mao-era legacy as partly positive, reject liberal democracy and 'universal values' as a Western template, and favour a strong, independent China.
scope: The mainstream of the 1990s to 2010s intellectual New Left in the PRC: Wang Hui, Cui Zhiyuan, Wang Shaoguang and Hu Angang, with the later statist turn (Jiang Shigong) noted. It is not the Western New Left of the 1960s, nor the Maoist fringe of Utopia and Nanjie Village, nor the liberal or Confucian camps; Maoist-wing positions are mentioned in notes. Many positions on non-Chinese issues are inferred and low confidence.

keyFigures.name: Wang Hui
keyFigures.role: Tsinghua intellectual historian, often called a leader of the New Left though he rejects the label.

keyFigures.name: Cui Zhiyuan
keyFigures.role: Political economist called the first 'New Left' figure, advocate of economic democracy and the Chongqing model.

keyFigures.name: Wang Shaoguang
keyFigures.role: Political scientist known for state-capacity and responsive-democracy arguments.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Wang Shaoguang frames the New Left case around human security and criticizes reform-era neglect of health care, so state-guaranteed care is a core demand.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Opposition to growing inequality and layoffs implies support for stronger wage floors, but wage floors are not a theme in the sources.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: New Leftists accept a market economy but reject neoliberal claims that markets alone serve society; Wang Hui separates a market from a market society.

public-ownership.rationale: Cui Zhiyuan holds that public ownership of assets complements private enterprise and praises Chongqing's multiplication of state assets; New Left opposes privatisation.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Concern with regional and class inequality implies progressive taxation, though the sources stress public asset revenue and land-value capture more than wealth taxes.

unions-good.rationale: Wang Hui sees socialist-era institutions as giving workers ways to contest unjust marketization, but independent unions are not an explicit New Left demand.

property-fundamental.rationale: Cui follows Mill in qualifying private property rights in the means of production and criticizes the property-rights discourse of liberals.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Critics of neoliberalism and global capital want market actors subordinated to social goals, though most emphasis is on state ownership rather than regulation.

cut-welfare.rationale: The New Left objects to the dismantling of security and the layoff of tens of millions of state workers, and Wang Shaoguang welcomes the turn back to welfare.

worker-ownership.rationale: Cui admires the Angang constitution's worker participation and Meade's labour-capital partnerships, though he stops short of pure worker ownership.

surveillance-ok.rationale: The statist wing defends state security against Western pressure; surveillance itself is not discussed, so this is inferred.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the strand's state-centred, socially conservative leanings.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Not addressed; the strand rejects liberal free-speech absolutism but has no stated position on hate speech.

strong-leader.rationale: The statist wing praises party-state capacity to act decisively, but the sources do not frame it as a strong-leader doctrine.

state-harmful.rationale: The New Left calls for greater state capacity, as in the Wang Shaoguang proposal for fiscal recentralization.

limit-guns.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from a state-centred outlook and the PRC's strict gun laws.

empower-police-military.rationale: Not addressed beyond great-power nationalism; adherents are not documented as demanding more police authority.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from socialist and conservative-leaning views of commodification.

decide-locally.rationale: Wang Shaoguang and Hu Angang argued that decentralization had weakened the state and called for fiscal centralization and inter-regional redistribution.

rehabilitation.rationale: Not addressed; no documented New Left line on penal philosophy.

traditional-family.rationale: Gan Yang and Han Deqiang pair left politics with cultural conservatism, but the family is not a central topic.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; adherents are split or silent.

abortion-legal.rationale: Not addressed; PRC law permits abortion and no New Left objection is documented.

more-religion-public.rationale: The sources never discuss religion's public role; a larger one is unlikely for a movement rooted in the secular socialist tradition, so this is a low-confidence inference.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Western racial-justice debates are not a documented New Left theme.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Not addressed; adherents draw on critical theory but no stated line.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Gan Yang and Han Deqiang stress cultural identity and Chinese civilizational distinctiveness against Western universals.

gradual-change.rationale: Wang Shaoguang praises incremental, experimental policy change, though the Maoist strand values revolution.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Immigration to China is negligible and the sources never raise it, so adherents have no documented stance and this leans on the movement's nationalism only weakly.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: The New Left sees Western human-rights advocacy and global institutions as vehicles of geopolitical pressure and Western hegemony.

free-trade.rationale: They are sceptical of neoliberalism and globalization as enabling capitalist colonization, favouring domestic demand and protection of the vulnerable.

nation-first.rationale: The movement wants China to act as a great power and criticizes weakness over territorial disputes.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: They treat Western human-rights advocacy as geopolitical pressure and reject universal-values justifications.

open-borders.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from nationalism and state-centred views.

limit-growth.rationale: They criticize growth at all costs but want to correct its distribution rather than cap it.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from support for state-led action against market failures.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: No documented line on technology; adherents split between modernizers and critics of modernity.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from state-led development and energy security preferences.

revolution-justified.rationale: Cui seeks to institutionalize Mao's 'righteous rebellion' and many view the revolutionary and Mao legacy positively, though the statist wing now defends the party.

experts-over-public.rationale: Wang Shaoguang wants ordinary people involved in the whole decision process, not only elites; the statist wing leans technocratic.

central-planning.rationale: Early New Left opposed the abandonment of five-year plans and supports state planning, but Cui and others defend a market-socialist mix.

socialized-markets.rationale: Cui Zhiyuan describes a socialist market economy in which socialised assets and markets work together, but his model keeps private enterprise alongside public ownership, so the 'as long as' condition is only partly met.

land-value-tax.rationale: Cui endorses Henry George's idea that society should capture land value increases and praises Chongqing's land-certificate exchange; replacing all taxes is George's scheme rather than a settled New Left demand.

tax-inheritance.rationale: No source mentions inheritance tax; a heavy levy follows from the movement's central concern with widening inequality, so it is inferred.

basic-income.rationale: Cui proposed a social dividend and a People's Permanent Trust Fund following Meade.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Opposition to neoliberal globalization and support for state-led development imply protection for domestic industry.

state-directs-investment.rationale: They favour state planning and the Chongqing model of government investment in housing, infrastructure and public assets.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Cui's liberal-socialist framing favours dispersed small property alongside public assets, but this is secondary to public ownership.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: New Leftists accept a market economy and do not demand abolition of money or wages.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Rejection of free-market ideology and support for state economic power make this strongly opposed.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Angang-style co-determination and labour-capital partnership are cooperative models, though not state-recognized price setting.

one-party-rule.rationale: Most New Leftists accept CCP leadership, and the statist wing calls the party the vehicle of socialism; Cui wants more intra-party democracy.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from republican and socialist commitments.

democracy-best.rationale: The New Left rejects competitive-election liberal democracy as the universal ideal, though Wang Shaoguang still claims a democratic ideal of responsiveness.

direct-votes.rationale: Wang Shaoguang stresses broader participation in decision-making, but he emphasizes mass line and responsiveness rather than referendums.

workers-councils.rationale: Angang participation is within enterprises, while political power is meant to stay with the party-state.

right-to-secede.rationale: Wang Hui is criticized for backing Zhou Enlai's denial of Tibetan self-determination, and the movement is nationalist about territory.

natural-rulers.rationale: Not addressed; egalitarian orientation points against, though the statist wing admires elite governance.

political-violence-never.rationale: Heirs of a revolutionary tradition that values Mao-era mass politics would not hold a pacifist rule.

war-builds-character.rationale: No source glorifies war as character-building; the movement's nationalism and great-power aims do not imply this romantic claim, so adherents lean against.

separate-church-state.rationale: The sources are silent on religion and the state; the secular socialist heritage and PRC practice suggest adherents accept strict separation, inferred only.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Scriptural law has no place in a Marxist-descended secular movement and nothing in the sources suggests otherwise, so this is a confident-direction but low-evidence inference.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Strong state capacity is a defining theme, so privatizing core state functions is rejected.

military-superiority.rationale: The movement wants China to be a great power and presses a firm line on territorial disputes.

ethnic-nation.rationale: The PRC framework is multi-ethnic; not documented as ethnonationalist.

class-struggle-history.rationale: They draw on Marxist and Maoist traditions, but sources do not make class conflict the central claim.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Wang Shaoguang says the New Left fought arguments that equality must be sacrificed to growth and values the egalitarian Mao decades despite poverty.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Minority and land questions in China are handled through state autonomy policy; the sources give no New Left view on indigenous land authority, so a neutral answer is used.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Anti-Western-hegemony outlook makes sympathy likely, but reparations are not discussed.

civilizational-union.rationale: The movement is oriented to China's own path and the sources show no interest in uniting nations by shared civilization, so a mild disagreement is inferred.

self-interest-moral.rationale: The movement criticizes market society and its logic of private gain.

duties-before-rights.rationale: The statist and Confucian-leaning wing prefers community over liberal individual rights.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: The sources do not address environmental ethics, and adherents differ between developmentalists and ecological critics of marketization, so this stays neutral.

limit-population.rationale: Not addressed; PRC policy context and inference from development planning.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: The movement seeks national development and modernization, not rejection of industry.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Inferred from emphasis on stability and social protection over disruption.

human-enhancement.rationale: Transhumanist bioethics is not a topic in New Left writing, so there is no basis for a position.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Algorithmic governance is absent from the sources, and the movement's emphasis on mass participation and responsiveness cuts both ways, so no position is inferred.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: The statist wing prizes state security capacity and sovereignty over information, so state-proof encryption is probably disfavoured, though the sources never address it.

restore-past-order.rationale: Adherents defend socialist achievements but pursue renewal, not restoration.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Wang Shaoguang praises pragmatic experimentation and Chongqing is pitched as an empirical test of ideas.

direct-action.rationale: Most work through the state or party; the Maoist fringe organizes protests.

means-match-ends.rationale: No source addresses prefigurative politics; Maoist and statist adherents would differ on this, so the answer is neutral.

return-to-foraging.rationale: The movement seeks development and modernization of China, so a return to hunter-gathering is plainly outside its program, though no source discusses it.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Cui values Mao-era blending of managers and workers under Angang, but does not call for abolition.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Egalitarian socialist heritage, but need-based distribution is not stated as a goal.

production-for-use.rationale: Opposition to marketization suggests sympathy, but the sources keep markets.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Critique of capitalist marketization, though most New Leftists do not assert a Marxian exploitation theory.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Adherents are split between Maoist enthusiasts and moderates who avoid the term.

collective-farming.rationale: Rural collectivization is part of the New Left program and Nanjie Village is praised as a model.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Dependency and world-systems ideas are used; Jiang casts US hegemony as imperial, but inevitability is not asserted.

taxation-theft.rationale: Cui praises state revenue from public assets and Wang Shaoguang urged fiscal centralization, so taxation is regarded as a legitimate tool for public goods and redistribution.

harm-principle.rationale: Liberal individual-liberty doctrines are rejected, though Cui cites Mill's liberal socialism.

individual-rights-only.rationale: They reject universal liberal values and treat rights as historically contingent.

conscription.rationale: The sources do not discuss conscription; great-power nationalism and PRC practice make acceptance of state military service the likely adherent view.

exit-over-voice.rationale: The idea that exit rather than voting checks government belongs to market-based thinking that the New Left, following Wang Hui's critique of market society, rejects.

state-as-business.rationale: They reject marketization of governance, per Wang Hui's market-society critique.

positive-liberty.rationale: Wang Hui argues liberals wrongly detach markets from social harms, and the movement ties freedom to material security and equality.

media-academia-power.rationale: The New Left criticizes elites and global capital, but nothing in the sources claims universities and media outrank elected officials, so mild disagreement is inferred.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Genetic racial hierarchies conflict with the egalitarian Marxist and anti-colonial heritage, though the sources do not address them.

organic-representation.rationale: Representation through families and trade bodies is a corporatist or conservative idea absent from New Left proposals, which centre on party-state responsiveness and mass participation.

total-state.rationale: They want strong state capacity but also economic participation and market elements, not totality.

national-rebirth.rationale: Jiang Shigong's narrative from Mao to Deng to Xi culminates in national strengthening, and the movement wants China as a great power.

territorial-expansion.rationale: They are assertive on disputed claims but do not advocate expansion.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Not addressed; feudal arrangements are alien to the program.

bound-labor.rationale: Serfdom-like obligations contradict the egalitarian socialist outlook and the movement's rural-equality agenda, though no source discusses them.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Wang Hui argues modernity and its universals are historically constructed and naturalized, and the movement treats universal values as contingent.

universal-morality.rationale: The movement rejects universal values as historically contingent and tied to Western interests.

single-common-good.rationale: The mass-line and party-as-vehicle outlook points toward a common interest, but not a stated philosophical thesis.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: China's New Left sources do not address Zionism, and adherents' anti-hegemony instincts do not map clearly onto the question.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: Diaspora return rights are not a topic in the sources, and no stance can be inferred from the movement's themes.

revive-national-language.rationale: Language revival is irrelevant to China's situation and the sources are silent, so no position is inferred.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Economic democracy and the Angang constitution's worker participation in management are central to Cui's program.

school-vouchers.rationale: Vouchers marketize schooling, which runs against the movement's critique of market society and preference for public provision, though education finance is not directly discussed.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: The Chongqing model leaned on heavy state investment, and Cui sought to lift domestic demand, so austerity-minded deficit avoidance is unlikely to be favoured.

economic-freedom.rationale: The New Left attacks the liberal link between markets and freedom and questions the notion that market reform restrains state power.

rule-by-example.rationale: The Maoist and Confucian-leaning strands favour moral leadership, but it is not a stated core.

national-self-determination.rationale: Anti-colonial in spirit but denied to minorities within China, so split.

force-without-un.rationale: Opposition to Western hegemony and unilateral pressure implies support for UN-based sovereignty norms.

reason-over-faith.rationale: The movement inherits a secular Marxist rationalism, but the sources do not discuss epistemology in these terms and Wang Hui questions Enlightenment universals, so support is mild.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: The sources only discuss welfare for Chinese citizens (including rural residents), so reserving benefits for citizens is the implicit assumption, with low confidence.

work-for-welfare.rationale: The sources do not discuss work requirements; the movement's egalitarian lean opposes punitive conditions but Mao-era work ethos pulls the other way, so it stays neutral.

class-collaboration.rationale: Cui's labour-capital partnership model envisions cooperation, though classes remain in the Marxist view.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Defenders of the Cultural Revolution's mass politics are not documented calling for destruction of culture.

dominated-front.rationale: Jiang describes a struggle against US hegemony and the movement opposes Western dominance.

workers-nation.rationale: Nationalism strongly marks the movement over proletarian internationalism.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Socialist heritage of gender equality; conservative strands unaddressed.

ban-interest.rationale: Adherents accept market finance within a socialist market economy and nothing in the sources suggests banning interest.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Legal racial segregation contradicts the egalitarian and anti-colonial self-understanding of the movement, though it is never addressed.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Marxist-influenced view, though the statist wing treats the party-state as a socialist instrument.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Energy mix is not discussed in the sources, so adherents have no documented stance.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Immigration and assimilation are not topics in New Left writing, so no position is documented.

elite-replacement.rationale: The replacement conspiracy is a Western far-right claim with no counterpart in New Left sources, which blame elites mainly for marketization and corruption.

proportional-representation.rationale: Wang Shaoguang dismisses competitive-election design as the core of democracy, so electoral formulas are not a concern and the answer is neutral.

national-mission.rationale: They reject exporting political models while promoting a distinct China model.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Gender analysis is not documented in the sources; New Left authors draw on Marxism and critical theory but leave no stated position.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Wang Hui argues special interest groups have seeped into state mechanisms, and the Chongqing model ran an anti-corruption campaign.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: The sources do not address eugenics, and the egalitarian heritage suggests mild opposition, so this is a low-confidence inference.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Cultural Revolution-era and state security legacies are defended by many; not documented.

night-watchman-state.rationale: The movement wants an enlarged, capable state for development and redistribution.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Opposition to race-mixing contradicts the socialist egalitarian outlook, though the sources never raise the question.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Egalitarian outlook, but the movement rejects liberal universalism in framing.

socialism-one-country.rationale: The movement endorses building socialism in China on its own road.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: Adherents' anti-colonial, anti-Western-hegemony stance suggests they would label settler states colonial, but this is inferred from general outlook.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: The PRC applies one civil code to all citizens and no New Left source argues for religious personal law, so uniformity is inferred.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Religious conversion is not discussed in the sources, so no position is inferred.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: Cattle slaughter is irrelevant to Chinese politics and is not mentioned in the sources, so mild disagreement is inferred from the movement's secular outlook.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: PRC state schools are secular and the movement's socialist secularism gives no reason to dissent, though the sources do not address it.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: The statist wing sees China's party-state as facing US hegemony and needing strength.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Wang Shaoguang wants responsive government, but the movement rejects electoral consent as the criterion.

trade-surplus.rationale: Cui argues for reducing export dependence by raising domestic demand, which cuts against a surplus aim.

population-transfer.rationale: Forced removal of minorities contradicts the movement's stated concern for stability and equality among non-Han areas, but it is never discussed.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Inferred from rejection of libertarianism and a revolutionary heritage.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: The movement's critique of market society and egalitarian aims oppose competition-as-progress doctrines, though the sources do not engage the claim directly.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: The statist wing defends the party's leading role against constitutionalist challenge, so banning parties aimed at the constitutional order is likely accepted, inferred.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: Inferred from critique of market domination, but not stated.

separated-powers.rationale: The New Left is often sceptical of constitutionalism and Western institutional checks.

vanguard-party.rationale: The statist New Left treats the party as the vehicle of socialism and Jiang makes communism the party's ideal.

priority-to-poor.rationale: The movement centres on inequality, regional underdevelopment and the interests of the poor and rural.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: Cui praises Chongqing's public rental housing, not sale to tenants.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Not addressed; adherents are split between labour sympathy and state order.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Wang and Hu argued that inequality is not fated and that policy matters.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Ethnic diversity and cohesion is not a documented New Left theme, and adherents would differ.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Wang Shaoguang notes that lot was historically democratic, but he does not call for it.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Emergency powers are not discussed in the sources, so adherents are treated as split between statist and participatory views.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Price controls for essentials fit the movement's state-intervention and anti-neoliberal economics, but the sources do not discuss them specifically.

party-controls-media.rationale: The statist wing accepts party-state leadership of information, but not a documented core demand.

party-commands-army.rationale: The statist New Left treats the CCP as the vehicle of socialism and the standard CCP principle is party command of the army, though the sources do not address it directly.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Naturalization policy is not a New Left topic, so no position is inferred.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Egalitarian concern and Mao-era ideals of cadres sharing workers' conditions suggest support, but it is not stated in the sources.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Democratic centralism is the party's model, which the statist wing supports.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: The movement stresses sovereignty and distrusts Western-led institutions, so pooling it in a supranational body is unlikely to appeal, inferred.

head-commands-forces.rationale: Executive command of the army is not discussed in the sources, so no position is inferred.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Church governance is irrelevant to the movement and unmentioned in the sources.

clerical-rule.rationale: Rule by religious scholars contradicts the secular socialist tradition, though no source discusses it.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Revolutionary defeatism conflicts with the strong nationalism and great-power aims documented for the movement.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Not addressed; split between statist and liberal-leaning adherents.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Term limits are not addressed by the sources, and adherents are split between party-state loyalists and critics, so no position is inferred.

recall-officials.rationale: Great Democracy ideals and mass-line responsiveness suggest openness.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: The movement's anti-hegemony framing, as in Jiang Shigong's account of US dominance, suggests sympathy for ending Western-led alliances, but this is inferred.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Cui praises Chongqing's public rental housing for low-income residents, so a ban on renting contradicts a documented policy.

people-in-arms.rationale: Maoist people's war is part of the tradition, but the mainstream New Left sources never propose replacing the army with an armed citizenry.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: New Left concern for the countryside is economic, about peasant income and inequality, not a moral preference for rural over urban life.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: The movement's territorial nationalism and demand for a firmer China suggest support for reunification, though the sources do not discuss Taiwan directly.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Anti-intellectual themes belong to Mao-era populism but are not documented in the intellectuals who define the New Left, so no position is taken.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Rejection of universal values and Western superiority suggests adherents would accept cultures as different rather than ranked, inferred.

death-penalty.rationale: The PRC applies capital punishment and the sources show no New Left opposition, so support is inferred for a statist movement.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Sex education is not discussed in New Left sources, and no stance can be inferred.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: A secular Marxist-influenced movement favours teaching evolution, though no source addresses creationism.

restrict-pornography.rationale: The sources do not discuss pornography; state-centred social outlook suggests acceptance of legal restriction, so mild agreement is inferred.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Citizenship rules are not discussed in the sources; PRC law is descent-based, so agreement is a weak inference.

minority-language-support.rationale: The West development policy seeks stability among non-Han areas, but language rights are not discussed.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Exemptions from general law for religious minorities run against the movement's statist outlook, though the sources do not address them.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: The movement is critical of liberal individualism and prioritizes social solidarity, so celebrating eccentricity is disfavoured, though not directly discussed.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: Anti-hegemony and dependency-theory sympathies suggest support for debt relief, but the sources do not mention it.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Cui's focus on economic democracy and the movement's critique of marketization imply that formal independence without economic transformation is hollow, inferred.

constituent-assembly.rationale: The movement is sceptical of constitutionalism and Western-style democratic procedures, so an elected constituent assembly is unlikely to be favoured.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Wang Shaoguang criticizes growth at all costs yet calls the authoritarian label useless.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Egalitarian concern with inequality extends to the world-system in dependency theory, so a duty of aid is plausible, though not stated.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Great-power nationalism and sovereignty emphasis make an independent deterrent natural, though nuclear policy is not addressed.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: Wang Shaoguang argues democracy cannot be equated with competitive elections, so direct presidential elections are not a priority.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Independent, price-stability-focused central banks embody the neoliberal orthodoxy that the New Left opposes, though central banks are not discussed directly.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Territorial nationalism and criticism of government weakness on disputes suggest adherents resist ceding claimed territory, inferred.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Cui, following Mill, qualifies private property in the means of production and favours public asset ownership.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: Not a New Left claim; they defend the broader socialist legacy.

precautionary-principle.rationale: The movement favours state action against market harms, so precautionary regulation fits, but environmental policy is not directly discussed.

collective-defense.rationale: Western collective-defense alliances are seen as vehicles of hegemony, so adherents are unlikely to endorse automatic mutual defense, inferred.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: This turns on specific cases and adherents' territorial nationalism cuts against a general principle, so no position is inferred.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: PRC practice places religious bodies under state supervision, and nothing in the sources suggests the New Left dissents, so agreement is inferred.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: A ceremonial head of state above parties is not discussed; adherents favour the party leading the state, so no position is inferred.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: The movement's territorial nationalism and the Tibet remark by Wang Hui imply support.

region-keeps-system.rationale: Wang Shaoguang sits on a Hong Kong strategic commission; not addressed directly.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Divine kingship contradicts the secular socialist outlook, though the sources never raise it.

flat-income-tax.rationale: A flat tax cuts against the movement's focus on inequality and redistribution, though tax design is not discussed in detail.

character-from-environment.rationale: The Marxist heritage treats social conditions as shaping people, but the sources do not discuss human nature explicitly, so only mild agreement is inferred.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: The sources do not discuss rulers' legal limits; adherents split between party-state loyalism and concern for accountability, so mild disagreement is inferred.

space-expansion.rationale: Space is not discussed in the sources, so there is no documented position.

mixed-constitution.rationale: Classical mixed-constitution theory is outside New Left debates, so no position is inferred.

leader-cult.rationale: Mao veneration is present on the Maoist fringe, but not in the mainstream intellectual New Left.

equal-parenting.rationale: Custody law is not a New Left topic, so no position is inferred.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: Cui values Mao's Cultural Revolution theory, though the movement does not endorse the claim as such.

land-redistribution.rationale: Rural egalitarianism and collective land ownership in the PRC suggest sympathy with giving land to those who farm it, though Chinese land is already redistributed, so this is inferred.

refugee-return.rationale: Refugee return rights are not discussed in the sources, so no position is inferred.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Claims based on co-nationals abroad are not documented in the sources, and the movement's claims rest on historic sovereignty, so mild disagreement is inferred.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Penalties for leaving a religion contradict the secular socialist stance, though the sources never raise it.

women-must-cover.rationale: Mandatory dress codes conflict with the movement's socialist gender-equality heritage, though not discussed.

common-currency.rationale: The movement emphasizes economic sovereignty and distrusts supranational integration, so a shared currency is mildly disfavoured, inferred.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Pan-ethnic unions of kin peoples are not part of New Left thinking, which is China-centred, so mild disagreement is inferred.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Cultural autonomy for minorities inside a state is not discussed by the sources, so no stance is inferred.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: This question about diaspora politics is not addressed in New Left writing, so no position is inferred.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: The movement draws on Marxist and world-systems traditions that stress material forces, but the sources do not state this directly, so mild agreement is inferred.

ban-cartels.rationale: Support for breaking up economic concentration fits the critique of capital power, but competition policy is not discussed, so it is inferred.

no-bailouts.rationale: Cui studied soft budget constraints yet favours state support.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: The movement is sceptical of constitutionalism and judicial constraint on popular will, so it leans toward majority supremacy, inferred.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: The socialist heritage of promoting women's representation suggests acceptance of quotas, but the sources do not discuss them.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Chongqing courted foreign investors like Hewlett-Packard and Foxconn, and the movement does not favour autarky, so a closed bloc is disfavoured.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Binding social standards in trade fit the movement's critique of neoliberal globalization, but the sources do not mention them.

moral-incentives.rationale: Mao-era moral incentives and the Angang constitution's cadre labour are admired by some strands, though the sources do not state it as program.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Foco-style insurgency is not part of the Chinese tradition the sources describe, and the mainstream New Left is not insurrectionary, so mild disagreement is inferred.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Egalitarian opposition to inherited advantage suggests agreement, but the sources do not mention titles or privileges.

history-own-civilization.rationale: The movement stresses Chinese civilizational distinctiveness and critiques Western historical narratives, so a nation-centred curriculum is inferred.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Anti-colonial and anti-hegemonic outlook makes adherents reject the idea of rule by advanced over backward societies.

patriotic-education.rationale: Nationalism and the statist wing's celebration of the party-state suggest support for patriotic schooling, though it is not discussed.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: American-style racial preferences are not a New Left topic, so no stance is documented.

public-money-creation.rationale: Support for a stronger state role in finance suggests sympathy for public money creation, but no source addresses it.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: The sources do not state whether capitalism can adapt; adherents differ between crisis theorists and those who accept markets.

former-empire-influence.rationale: The sources do not discuss cultivating influence in formerly imperial regions, so no position is inferred.

delink-world-market.rationale: Chongqing invited foreign investors and Cui co-edited a book on China and globalization.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: The theory of exploited poor countries and complicit rich-country workers is not stated in the New Left sources, so no position is inferred.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Libertarian freedom of association conflicts with the movement's egalitarianism and critique of market society, though it is not discussed.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: The New Left is often sceptical of constitutionalism and entrenched Western-style rights limits on government.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: Anti-colonial grievances over unequal treaties are part of Chinese nationalism, so adherents likely reject the binding force of such treaties, inferred.

elective-rulers.rationale: Wang Shaoguang stresses accountability and responsiveness, which supports non-hereditary rule, though he does not insist on election.

minority-veto.rationale: A single-member veto contradicts the movement's majoritarian mass-line outlook and statist preference for decisive governance, though not discussed.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Adherents are split between party-state loyalists and those sympathetic to rightful resistance, and the sources do not address it.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Parliamentary sovereignty versus monarchy is not discussed, and the movement rejects Western parliamentary models as universal, so neutral.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Animal welfare is not addressed by the sources, and a general acceptance of animal suffering as morally relevant is assumed in low confidence.

animal-use-humane.rationale: Humane animal use is a mainstream default view that no New Left source challenges, so agreement is inferred.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Aristocratic duty is a conservative concept absent from the sources, but egalitarians would affirm obligations of the wealthy toward the poor, inferred.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Withdrawal from public affairs contradicts the movement's activist engagement and its emphasis on mass participation.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: The New Left draws on critical theory and its critique of market society, so adherents would accept this, though the claim is not stated in the sources.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: New Left authors draw on Gramsci and critical theory, which stress consent through culture, but the sources do not state it explicitly.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: The New Left draws on dependency and world-systems theory, which hold that peripheral countries' surplus flows to the core.

native-born-offices.rationale: Reserving offices for native-born citizens is not discussed in the sources, so no position is inferred.

party-own-road.rationale: Socialism with Chinese characteristics; Jiang's Party narrative.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Maoist self-reliance heritage and Cui's emphasis on domestic demand suggest agreement, though foreign investment is welcomed in practice.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Territorial nationalism and criticism of weakness over disputes imply support for demanding return of lost territory, but it is inferred.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: Indigenous leadership over settler descendants is not discussed in New Left sources, so no position is inferred.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: The Marxist heritage values anti-fascism, but constitutional design is not a New Left topic, so only mild agreement is inferred.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: The movement views Mao's legacy as largely positive and treats Cold War equivalence as Western ideology, so adherents reject condemning communism like fascism.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: American Civil War historiography is not discussed, and the movement's Marxist influence makes it likely to treat slavery as central, inferred.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Monument debates are not a documented New Left topic, so there is no position.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: Men's issues are not addressed in New Left sources, so there is no stated position.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: Gender violence services are not a documented New Left topic, so no position is inferred.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: The movement rejects universal values and the exportability of Western institutions.

military-guardian-role.rationale: The statist wing places the army under party command rather than as an independent guardian, so a political guardian role for the army is disfavoured.

paid-care-work.rationale: Socialist feminist ideas of valuing care work fit the heritage, but the sources do not mention it, so support is a weak inference.

filial-duty.rationale: Mao-era New Left thought criticized Confucian hierarchy while some later statist writers embraced tradition; the sources show no settled line, so split.

office-by-exam.rationale: Later statist New Left writers such as Jiang Shigong favour a meritocratic party-state, but the mainstream stresses mass participation; inferred.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: The New Left criticizes subordination to global capital and defends public ownership and national economic independence.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Socialist-era Chinese law already allowed divorce by mutual consent and the New Left took no conservative family line; inferred.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Wang Shaoguang's responsive-democracy argument and Mao-era mass-line and Paris Commune themes favour accountability to the masses, but recall by electors is not explicit; inferred.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: The New Left attacks reform-era privatization and wants state-guaranteed social security; Wang Shaoguang stresses state-funded human security.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Cui Zhiyuan defends collective and public land ownership and land value capture, in line with Chinese state land tenure.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: The New Left rejects electoral-parliamentary democracy as a Western template while stressing accountability; no position on budget approval is documented, so split.

single-official-language.rationale: The New Left backs a strong unified state and Wang Hui's Tibet remark opposes separatism, but language policy is not discussed; inferred.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: State or collective land ownership and economic independence imply that foreigners should not own land; inferred.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: The New Left frames inequality mainly in class and regional terms rather than racial group disparities and rejects imported Western categories; inferred.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: The New Left criticizes market society, inequality and consumer culture of the reform era; inferred from its critique rather than a direct quotation.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: The New Left champions Chinese independence and non-interference and criticizes Western interventions; inferred.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Opposition to hegemony and defence of sovereignty imply rejecting great-power interventions to hold a bloc together; the Soviet precedent was not addressed in the sources. Inferred.

corporate-influence.rationale: The New Left criticizes reform-era privatization and subordination to global capital, so it treats concentrated corporate power over policy as a core problem.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: Inferred from its embrace of state capacity and its rejection of Western templates; foreign-funded civil society is not directly addressed.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Population policy is not addressed in the sources; inferred as split between state-planning and equity-focused views.

residents-only-property.rationale: Not addressed; its rural and regional equity concerns point one way and its market-economy acceptance the other, so inferred as split.

job-guarantee.rationale: Inferred from its defence of public ownership, state capacity and economic democracy; a job guarantee is not a documented demand.

democratic-peace.rationale: It rejects liberal democracy and 'universal values' as a Western template, so it would doubt that spreading democracy brings peace. Inferred.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Inferred: it embraces a strong state and the Chinese legal order, so a general denial of any duty to obey is unlikely.

non-intervention.rationale: Inferred from its call for a strong, independent China that resists Western pressure.

industrial-unions.rationale: Inferred from its economic-democracy and pro-worker orientation; industrial organization of workers fits it, but union form is not documented.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Nothing in its documented positions casts a minority as a conspiring enemy; inferred rejection.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: Inferred: it is a socialist-statist current with no programme to abolish legal marriage.

public-access-to-information.rationale: Not addressed directly; Wang Shaoguang's interest in accountability fits it, but the state-centred outlook cuts against, so inferred as split.

local-production.rationale: Inferred from its concern for rural and regional equity and criticism of global-capital integration.

informal-organisation.rationale: It embraces the state and institutional capacity, the opposite of informal, anti-party organization. Inferred.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Inferred from its statist turn and defence of national independence against Western norms.

religious-nation.rationale: It works within a socialist framework with no religious definition of the nation. Inferred.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: Inferred from the New Left's insistence on an independent China and rejection of Western templates; ritual submission to a leading power is not a theme.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: Inferred from its emphasis on equality and state capacity to equalise regions; pooling revenue across regions fits, though it is not discussed directly.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: The New Left defends public ownership of productive assets within a socialist framework, while keeping ordinary private life and consumption.

defeat-communism.rationale: Inferred: adherents defend socialism and the Mao-era legacy, so they would not want communism defeated.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: Wang Shaoguang and others criticise reform-era privatisation of health and social services and defend state provision.

religion-illusion.rationale: Inferred from its Marxist-influenced secular outlook; religion is not a theme in the sources.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Cui's liberal socialism treats market institutions as useful building blocks while criticising capitalism; inferred from that, since a verdict on capitalism's history is not stated.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: Inferred from the Mao-era socialist record on women's equality and its critique of reform-era inequality; not stated in the sources.

socialized-care.rationale: Inferred from the favourable view of Mao-era collective services and its case for public provision; domestic work is not addressed.

purge-loanwords.rationale: Language purism is not a New Left theme; inferred from a cosmopolitan intellectual culture that engages Western theory.

treaties-binding.rationale: Inferred from its support for a strong unitary state; treaties with internal nations are not a theme.

cooperative-communities.rationale: The mainstream keeps a market economy under a strong state; communal self-governing communities are a Maoist-wing idea, noted in the audit.

majority-settlement.rationale: Inferred: Han settlement policy is not discussed by the mainstream, which stresses equity for minority and poor regions.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Cui's liberal socialism and the New Left aim to redefine socialism as a course beyond both capitalism and Soviet-style planning.

historical-land-claim.rationale: The New Left defends China's territorial integrity and a historical claim to Taiwan and other territory; inferred as it is not their core topic.

holocaust-denial.rationale: No part of the New Left treats the Holocaust as fiction; inferred from mainstream scholarship.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Homosexuality was decriminalised in China in 1997 and the New Left has no stated aim of restoring a ban; inferred.

suppress-opposition.rationale: The statist turn (s4) favours order, but Wang Shaoguang (s3) argues for democratisation, so adherents split.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: The New Left works inside a secular socialist framework and does not seek punishment of blasphemy; inferred.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: As a critique of global capital and Western domination, it opposes colonial exploitation; inferred.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: Not an issue the New Left addresses; as a secular current it would not hold this as a duty of faith. Inferred.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: A secular current that rejects religious authority over the state; inferred.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Cui Zhiyuan advocates economic democracy and worker participation (s2), and Wang Shaoguang argues for public participation in decisions (s3).

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: The New Left frames inequality mainly as class and regional inequality, and is often sceptical of Western identity politics; inferred.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Not a New Left concern, and its critique of Western liberal templates makes it cool toward the issue; inferred.

assisted-dying.rationale: The New Left has not addressed it; adherents split. Inferred.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: Cui Zhiyuan seeks institutional innovation beyond capitalism-versus-socialism, but the current as a whole keeps a socialist label; adherents split.

alienated-labor.rationale: Marxist-influenced critique of reform-era marketisation (s1, s7) implies the alienation view; inferred.

islam-incompatible.rationale: It rejects 'universal values' as a Western template, but does not frame this as civilisational incompatibility; inferred.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: A secular current that rejects religious authority over the state; inferred.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: In the secular PRC state, officials wear no religious dress and the New Left does not contest this; inferred.

ban-nda-harassment.rationale: Its critique of reform-era power imbalances favours protecting employees against employers; inferred.

social-market-economy.rationale: It keeps a market economy inside a socialist framework with public ownership and welfare (s1), though it does not use this label.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: The New Left calls for a strong, independent China and state capacity (s1, s4); inferred.

rich-first.rationale: It criticises the reform era's inequality and the regional gaps that came from letting some get rich first.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: It favours a strong, independent China, which implies keeping outside rival blocs; inferred.

dynastic-succession.rationale: The New Left defends a socialist republic and rejects hereditary rule; this follows from its repudiation of monarchy and its egalitarian commitments.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: Cui's economic democracy favours state and public control of finance over user-owned mutual banks; the specific issue is not discussed, so inferred.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: The New Left faults reform-era subordination to global capital and international institutions and favours a strong, independent China setting its own course.

property-franchise.rationale: The New Left stresses equality and economic democracy and would reject wealth-based voting restrictions.

domination-women-nature.rationale: Its Marxist and Maoist heritage includes critiques of exploitation of nature and women, but the linkage is not a core theme; inferred.

reification.rationale: Wang Hui draws on Western Marxist critique of commodification and depoliticization, which fits the claim that market forces appear to rule people.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: The New Left's critique of capitalism extends to market power over media, but it also rejects liberal press freedom as a template.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: Wang Hui and Jiang Shigong criticise liberal legalism and defend party-state discretion, though some adherents favour rule of law; contested.

racial-franchise.rationale: The New Left treats China as a multiethnic state and rejects ethnic nationhood, so an ethnic franchise has no place.

online-participation.rationale: Cui Zhiyuan promotes deliberative and participatory democracy, so online participation fits; inferred, with state control of the internet as a caveat.

open-government-data.rationale: Wang Shaoguang's responsiveness and accountability model implies publishing how proposals were handled; inferred.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: The state is officially secular and the New Left defends that; limits on interfaith marriage are not a theme, so inferred.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: Targeting a religious minority's shops contradicts its ideal of ethnic and religious unity within one state; inferred.

citizens-assembly.rationale: New Left writers favour state capacity and economic democracy within the party-state framework and reject Western-style democratic templates, so lot-based assemblies are not a standard demand. Inferred.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: The New Left is largely secular and focused on political economy; it has no settled stance on reforming religious doctrine. Inferred from that silence.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: The New Left criticizes reform-era inequality and the power of capital, and wants public ownership and regional equity to restrain concentrated wealth.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: The mainstream New Left did not address this; Maoist and nationalist wings lean conservative, others do not, so it is treated as split.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: The state is officially atheist but the New Left focuses on economics, and inferred from its secular socialist framework it does not oppose religion actively.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: The New Left stresses state capacity and the Chinese party-state, and nothing suggests abolishing police or prisons; inferred.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: It defends a unified, centralized state and rejects Western templates of liberal democracy; inferred.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: The New Left argues for strong public provision of health, education and welfare and criticizes reform-era retreat of the state.

term-limits.rationale: Not discussed by the New Left; it criticizes liberal democracy but also reform-era elite entrenchment, so no clear lean.

vote-delegation.rationale: It rejects liberal democracy and Western procedural templates, and favours responsiveness to people's needs over voting mechanisms; inferred.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: Not discussed in New Left writing; inferred to have no clear lean.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: Not discussed; religious leadership lies outside the New Left's concerns.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: The socialist tradition it draws on promotes gender equality, but the New Left did not take up this issue; inferred.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: Inferred from the New Left's statist, sovereignty-minded view of citizenship; local suffrage for foreigners is not discussed.

rent-control.rationale: Inferred from its criticism of market-driven inequality and defence of state capacity in housing and welfare; rent caps are not specifically discussed.

abolish-ip.rationale: Inferred: the New Left criticises subordination to global capital, which includes the IP regime, but it does not call for abolition and defends a market economy within a socialist framework.

uniformed-youth.rationale: Inferred: mass drilled youth movements are not part of the New Left programme, though the Maoist wing and later statists admire mobilisation.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: Inferred: the New Left wants an independent, strong China, and PRC possession of nuclear weapons is taken for granted, but basing on territory is not discussed.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: Inferred from its stress on national independence and opposition to subordination to Western powers.

recognise-genocide.rationale: Inferred: the New Left is sceptical of Western moral universalism, yet nothing in the sources addresses formal genocide recognition.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: The New Left defends public ownership and criticises privatisation and inequality, which fits rewarding work over property ownership.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Inferred: the New Left has no pacifist commitment and defends state power and national defence; not discussed directly.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: Inferred: the statist turn and the Mao-era legacy it honours stress a continuous Chinese civilisation-state, though the older New Left is mainly concerned with modernity.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: Gender theory is not addressed by the mainstream New Left; adherents are not known to hold a settled view.

no-fixed-category-of-women.rationale: Gender politics is outside the doctrine and the sources do not address it.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: Inferred: the Mao-era legacy and national revival the New Left defends include honouring revolutionary martyrs, though not as saints.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: Inferred: the New Left frames politics in terms of class, institutions and development, not as a spiritual struggle between good and evil.

homeland-cultural-centre.rationale: Inferred: it is concerned with the Chinese state and mainland development, not with a diaspora; not discussed.

culture-before-state.rationale: Inferred: the New Left prioritises economic and political institution-building and state capacity over cultural renewal.

god-not-male.rationale: Religion and the gender of God are outside the New Left's concerns.

scripture-judged-by-women.rationale: Religious texts are not a New Left topic and the sources do not address it.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: Inferred: the New Left favours public ownership and equity among regions and groups rather than ethnic control of the economy; not stated directly.

single-unit-for-people.rationale: Inferred: the New Left defends the PRC's unitary state with regional autonomy within it and has no programme of ethnic territorial merger.

independent-unions.rationale: New Left writers defend the party-state's role; independent unions are not a prominent demand. Inferred.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: Cui Zhiyuan and Wang Shaoguang argue for economic democracy and mass participation, building on the Mao-era legacy, though within a party-led state.

local-essentials-public.rationale: The New Left defends public ownership and criticises privatization.

second-chamber.rationale: Not addressed; the PRC is unicameral and New Left authors reject Western institutional templates.

municipal-property.rationale: Cui Zhiyuan praised community-owned township enterprises, but the camp mainly defends state and public ownership, so adherents split.

confederal-coordination.rationale: The New Left favours a strong central state and state capacity; inferred.

family-wage.rationale: Concern for equity and workers suggests support; inferred.

faster-drug-approval.rationale: Not addressed by the New Left.

ageing-research-funding.rationale: Not addressed by the New Left.

anonymous-payments.rationale: State capacity emphasis suggests opposition to untraceable money; inferred.

online-anonymity.rationale: Statist turn suggests acceptance of state oversight of online identity; inferred.

person-over-state.rationale: It criticises liberal individualism and puts collective and state goals first; inferred.

spiritual-nature.rationale: Secular Marxist-influenced intellectuals; inferred, not discussed in the sources.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: Unitary-state tradition makes regional powers delegated by the centre; inferred.

gm-crops.rationale: Not addressed by New Left writers, so no position can be inferred from their principles.

dense-cities.rationale: Not addressed by New Left writers, so no position can be inferred from their principles.

racial-group-interests.rationale: Class rather than race frames its politics; inferred.

racial-pride.rationale: Not addressed; Han-centred nationalism is not part of its mainstream.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: It favours a strong, independent China and distrusts Western interventions; inferred.

language-defines-nation.rationale: Inferred: the New Left defends the multi-ethnic PRC state and its unity, not a nation defined by language across state borders.

communal-electorates.rationale: Inferred from its statist, unitary framework and commitment to a common civic project; separate religious electorates are not discussed.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: Inferred from its call for a strong, independent China and wariness of Western pressure and global capital; plots are not a central theme.

free-public-college.rationale: Inferred from its defence of public provision and criticism of reform-era marketization of education, health and housing.

pollution-taxes.rationale: Inferred: the New Left stresses state planning and inequality over environmental pricing, and sources do not discuss pollution taxes.

future-generations.rationale: Inferred from the sustainability and human-security themes in Wang Shaoguang and Hu Angang; not explicit in the sources.

women-distinct-values.rationale: The New Left sources do not address gendered values; adherents are not known to take a common line.

arms-reduction.rationale: Inferred: it wants a strong, independent China but criticizes militarism less than inequality; the sources do not address arms levels.

open-diplomacy.rationale: Inferred from its statist outlook and its defence of state autonomy in foreign affairs; openness of treaties is not discussed.

capital-controls.rationale: It criticizes reform-era subordination to global capital and defends state capacity to manage the economy, which favours state control over capital flows.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: Inferred from its emphasis on state capacity and a strong independent China.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: Inferred from its nationalism and its support for a strong state; the topic is not addressed in its texts.

collective-bargaining.rationale: Its defence of economic democracy, labour protection and equality implies workers bargaining collectively.

in-work-tax-credits.rationale: Inferred from its call for redistribution and rural and regional equity; the instrument is not discussed.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: Inferred from its criticism of neoliberal reform and its stress on state capacity to spend.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: It criticizes the subordination of China to global capital and favours a fairer international order.

smash-state-machine.rationale: Its later statist turn embraced the party-state as the vehicle for its goals, rejecting the idea of smashing it.

free-economic-experiment.rationale: Cui Zhiyuan champions local experimentation, as in Chongqing, and institutional pluralism in forms of ownership.

nature-as-capital.rationale: Inferred from its socialist, public-ownership stance; pricing nature is not discussed.

sacred-nation.rationale: Its nationalism and defence of a strong China suggest valuing the nation as an enduring community; inferred.

student-debt-relief.rationale: Inferred from its egalitarian, anti-neoliberal stance; not discussed in the sources.

internal-colonialism.rationale: Its focus on regional and rural equity and critique of reform-era gaps fits this idea, though it uses other terms; inferred.

shared-human-nature.rationale: It rejects 'universal values' as a Western template, so a fixed universal human nature grounding rights is inferred to be doubted.

public-service-media.rationale: It rejects liberal media norms and favours a strong party-state, so independent media free of government control is inferred to be opposed.

religions-one-truth.rationale: New Left writers are secular and focus on political economy; the PRC's official line is non-committal on religious truth, so inferred as indifferent.

farm-price-support.rationale: The New Left criticizes reform-era rural neglect and favours rural equity and state support for the countryside; Wang Shaoguang and Hu Angang press for state protection of farmers.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: The New Left favours a strong, independent China, so keeping deterrents is inferred; the texts discuss strategy, not nuclear policy.

workers-own-party.rationale: The New Left works within the existing Party-state framework and favours economic democracy rather than a new party; an independent workers' party is inferred as unlikely.

ban-fgm.rationale: The PRC bans FGM-type harms in principle and the New Left stresses state protection of the vulnerable; not discussed in sources, inferred.

women-property-inheritance.rationale: The New Left backs equity and PRC law grants women equal inheritance, so equal land rights are inferred, though the sources do not discuss it.

one-language-many-names.rationale: Inferred from the New Left's Han-centred national outlook and the PRC's stress on one national language, Putonghua; the varieties are regarded as dialects of Chinese.

pollution-tort-liability.rationale: The New Left prefers state capacity and public ownership to private-law settlement, so agency regulation is inferred over private suits.

customary-chiefs-lawmaking.rationale: The New Left supports a strong centralized state and rejects liberal-democratic template; a formal role for chiefs is inferred as unwelcome.

environment-over-liberty.rationale: The New Left criticizes market-driven growth and defends state intervention against global capital; priority of environment over liberty is inferred.

mandatory-sentences.rationale: The New Left favours state authority and stability over liberal procedural rights; fixed sentences are inferred from that.

immigrants-learn-language.rationale: Inferred from the New Left's national-sovereignty outlook and the PRC's promotion of the national language; no source addresses immigrants.

no-compulsory-union.rationale: New Left writers defend workers' rights and unions' role in economic democracy, so compulsory membership is not opposed in principle; inferred.

voter-id.rationale: The New Left has not addressed voter ID, since it distrusts competitive electoral politics generally; inferred as neutral.

religious-equal-recognition.rationale: The New Left is mostly secular and has not argued about legal precedence among religious interpretations; inferred.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: Wang Shaoguang argues that equating democracy with competitive elections is too narrow, and the New Left rejects liberal procedural democracy as a Western template.

premarital-sex.rationale: The New Left is secular and socially permissive in line with PRC social change, though it has little to say on sexual ethics; inferred.

internet-shutdowns.rationale: Internet shutdowns were not a New Left topic; adherents defend a strong state but are not recorded on this; inferred as split.

negative-income-tax.rationale: The New Left criticizes market-oriented welfare reform and defends state-guaranteed provision; a cash payment replacing welfare programs is inferred as disfavoured.

women-suffrage.rationale: Women's equal political rights are part of the PRC socialist inheritance the New Left defends, and no writer in the sources questions them.

religion-oppresses-women.rationale: Marxist-inflected writers would tie oppression to class more than religion, and the New Left did not address it; inferred as neutral.

race-social-construct.rationale: Marxist-socialist tradition in the PRC treats race as a historical product; the New Left did not address it directly, so this is inferred.

gender-equality-agencies.rationale: The PRC maintains the state-run All-China Women's Federation inherited from Mao-era socialism, which the New Left generally defends; inferred.

homestead-ownership.rationale: Inferred from its defence of public ownership and criticism of privatization; it has no stated view on first-claim property.

international-criminal-courts.rationale: Inferred from its stress on Chinese independence and rejection of Western 'universal values' as a template.

scripture-inerrant.rationale: Inferred: a secular Marxist-influenced current with no stated position on scripture.

gendered-self-government.rationale: Inferred: it has no stated line on gendered self-government and its focus is class and development.

defend-planned-state.rationale: Inferred from its defence of public ownership and state capacity, though the mainstream keeps a market economy and the Maoist wing is stronger on this.

indirect-election.rationale: Inferred from its acceptance of the PRC congress system and its rejection of liberal electoral democracy as a template.

national-church-status.rationale: Inferred: a secular current with no stated interest in privileged status for a national church.

minority-territorial-autonomy.rationale: Inferred: the PRC's regional ethnic autonomy system is the established framework it works within, though it is not a core New Left theme.

disputed-territory-plebiscite.rationale: Inferred from its strong-state, national-unity stance on Taiwan and frontier regions.

keep-colonial-borders.rationale: Inferred from its emphasis on a strong, independent state and the PRC's own stance on inherited borders.

simple-living.rationale: Inferred: its critique of consumerism and inequality is not a call for simple living, and adherents are not agreed.

restrict-indigenous-settlement.rationale: Inferred: no stated position, and it sits uneasily with both regional equity and national unity.

equal-conscription.rationale: Inferred: no stated position on conscription, and adherents are not agreed.

homeland-spiritual-bond.rationale: The New Left stresses national independence and Chinese modernity, not an ancestral-land bond, and some strands are skeptical of cultural nationalism; inferred.

extrajudicial-killing.rationale: The New Left defends state capacity and the Mao-era legacy but not extrajudicial executions of drug suspects; the topic is not addressed and this is inferred.

close-ties-china.rationale: The New Left favors a strong, independent China, which implies less reliance on the United States, but it does not focus on foreign partners; inferred.

protect-kin-minorities.rationale: The New Left does not address China's ethnic kin abroad and the statement has little relevance for its Chinese state focus; inferred.

resources-common-ownership.rationale: Its defense of public ownership and economic democracy implies shared claims to resources, though not a Georgist compensation scheme; inferred.

self-ownership.rationale: The New Left's collectivist critique of market individualism and liberal rights implies skepticism of full self-ownership; inferred.

cut-consumption-tax.rationale: The New Left wants more redistribution and rural equity, which could favor cutting regressive taxes, but it has no stated line on consumption taxes; inferred.

targeted-social-spending.rationale: Wang Shaoguang and others argue for universal public health care and security against reform-era marketization and means-tested targeting.

bypass-parties-groups.rationale: The New Left generally defends the Party and the state as the vehicles of popular will, and some such as Wang Shaoguang favor mass participation through them; inferred.

no-business-privileges.rationale: The New Left criticizes reform-era privatization that enriched the well-connected and insiders, so ending special privileges fits its critique.

no-denominational-politics.rationale: As a secular, PRC-based current it accepts the state's ban on religiously organised politics; inferred.

tech-with-ancestral-values.rationale: Adherents are split between modernist and Mao-era revolutionary stances and cultural-traditionalist ones; inferred.

wife-divorce-without-consent.rationale: Mao-era marriage law established women's right to divorce and the New Left does not challenge it; inferred.

national-resource-control.rationale: The New Left criticizes subordination to global capital and defends public ownership and state control of strategic assets.

missingStatements.text: Democracy should be judged by how responsive government is to people's needs, not only by whether leaders are chosen in competitive elections.
missingStatements.rationale: Wang Shaoguang defines democracy as responsibility, responsiveness and accountability and argues that equating it with competitive elections is too narrow.

missingStatements.text: The first three decades of the People's Republic left a legacy of equality, literacy and public health that outweighs its failures.
missingStatements.rationale: The New Left generally views Mao's legacy as fundamentally positive, crediting literacy, education, health and self-reliance despite its failings.
missingStatements.declined: A verdict on one country's history rather than a question other ideologies can take a side on in neutral words; the underlying stance is covered by central-planning and state-directs-investment.

missingStatements.text: Ordinary workers should take part in managing the enterprises where they work, and managers in productive labour.
missingStatements.rationale: Cui cites the Angang constitution's two participations as proof that co-determination and economic democracy are native to China; the bank's workplace-democracy statement only partly captures managerial labour.

notes: The label is contested and many named thinkers reject it. Early New Left (Cui, Wang Hui) sought to redefine socialism and kept critical distance from the state; the later statist wing (Jiang Shigong, Wang Shaoguang) backs the party-state and China model; a Maoist wing (Han Deqiang, Utopia, Nanjie Village) is more hostile to markets and favours rural collectivization and the Cultural Revolution's mass politics. The profile follows the intellectual mainstream; Maoists would answer more strongly on class struggle, collectivization and leader veneration.
